sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $332 billion in FY2026, and operating income compounded faster, at 20.5% a year [F1][F10][F221][F223].
FY2018 was the sharpest break, with net margin falling 11.4pp to 15.0% [D62][F62], before FY2019 rebounded 16.2pp to 31.2% [D115][F63].
The filing ties the FY2018 hit to a charge for the TCJA enactment in that year's second quarter, which lifted the effective tax rate to 54.6% [P61][D32].
Operating margin rose 4.6pp to 41.6% in FY2021, and the filing credits a change in server and network equipment useful lives for the gross margin rise that year [D220][F45][P51][D219].
Intelligent Cloud contributed 11.2pp of FY2026's 17.8% revenue growth [D917][D472].
Server products and cloud services grew 31.5% and added 11.0pp, which the filing attributes to Azure, where growth was 41% [D641][D642][P12].

Operating expenses rose 7.4% against 17.8% revenue growth, a 53.3% incremental margin, and the filing ties the cost growth to AI compute, talent and data, and an XBOX impairment [D491][D472][D498][P16].
Diluted EPS grew 31.6%, slightly ahead of net income at 31.3% and operating income at 20.8%, with the share count down 0.2% [D476][D474][D473][D493].
Other income rose to $10.7 billion from a $4.90 billion loss, which the filing traces mainly to $6.5 billion of OpenAI-related net gains [X124][X123][P7].
Operating margin of 46.8% sits at its window high, against a window median of 41.7% and a low of 30.1% [F50][D974][D975][D973].
Gross margin fell 0.9pp to 67.9%, and cost of revenue cut the operating margin by 0.9pp, which other lines more than offset with a 1.2pp gain [D486][F30][D500][D502].
Intelligent Cloud's operating margin slipped to 41.3% from 42.0%, and the filing ties its lower gross margin percentage to AI infrastructure and Azure mix shift [D963][D962][P11].
The effective tax rate rose to 19.4% from 17.6%, which the filing attributes to the mix of U.S. and foreign earnings [D458][D404][P5].
Operating cash flow of $183 billion was 1.37x net income, but free cash flow of $67.0 billion was 0.50x, equal to the window low [F100][D459][F120][D460][D988].

Capital expenditure of $116 billion was 34.9% of revenue and 3.38x depreciation and amortisation, leaving the free cash flow margin at 20.2% against a window median of 30.3% [F110][D455][D461][X74][D456][D984].

The filing attributes the $66.9 billion rise in cash used in investing mainly to a $51.4 billion increase in property and equipment additions, while operating cash flow rose 34.4% on higher customer receipts [P1][D477].
Net cash rose to $72.9 billion from $66.8 billion, 22.0% of revenue, and ranks at the 83rd percentile of six software peers against a median of -7.2% [D465][D411][D466][D1006][D1007].
In FY2024 cash and investments fell 25.6% as cash used in investing rose to $97.0 billion, mainly on acquisitions of companies [D386][F128][P23].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion and dividends of $26.4 billion absorbed 72.7% of free cash flow, and diluted shares fell only 0.2% [X147][X157][D468][D493].
The payout is covered, but with conversion at 0.50x [D460] there is little headroom after capex.
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2025 and FY2026 [R1], at 0.70x [D406] and 0.50x [D460], as free cash flow fell 6.5% [D478].
Gross margin has fallen in two straight years, by 0.9pp in FY2025 [D432] and 0.9pp in FY2026 [D486], which the filing ties to AI infrastructure costs [P11].
Net income growth of 31.3% [D474] outran operating income growth of 20.8% [D473] because of OpenAI-related gains [P7].
That step-up is partly non-operating, so operating margin is the cleaner trend.
FY2017 pre-tax income, tax and receivables were restated after first filing [R2][R3][R4], so FY2017 ratios are excluded from this analysis.
Free cash flow margin recovering toward the 30.3% window median [D984] from 20.2% [D456] would confirm capex is being absorbed, while a further fall would extend the [R1] pattern in the FY2027 10-K.

Other income staying above the FY2026 level of $10.7 billion [X124] would confirm the OpenAI gains recur, while a slide toward the $4.90 billion FY2025 loss [X123] would widen the gap between net margin of 40.3% [F70] and operating margin of 46.8% [F50] in the FY2027 10-K.
